# Git sidebar action conformance cases

These language-neutral examples support `Documentation/design/2026-11-27-git-sidebar-actions-prd.md` and sprint #145. They are test inputs and expected outcomes, not production code or a client protocol. Each `id` must be consumed and asserted by each independent platform test suite; unknown cases must fail rather than be silently skipped. The descriptive `given`, `action`, and `expected` fields define observable behavior rather than Git command sequences. `f`, `g`, etc. are literal repository-relative fixture names; `base`, `staged`, `dirty`, `more`, `new`, and `other` are distinct file bytes. HEAD and index values are explicitly stated when relevant. Stashes N and O are distinct Git entries; other changes are unchanged unless explicitly described.

Platform adapters create isolated disposable repositories, commits, files and linked worktrees for the cases, record content/index/status and stash identity/order, execute the native action, and compare the full affected and unaffected state. Use deterministic barriers for stale-confirmation and apply/removal races. Error-injection is permitted for process failures/races, but real Git and filesystem integration are mandatory for normal semantics. Do not use the developer's checkout as a fixture. Cases that describe refused commands must assert no file, index or ref mutation. Race cases must never be read as proof an app lock prevents an external Git process.

Both clients must also test literal pathspecs, newlines/Unicode where supported by the target filesystem, directory symlinks and line endings, unrelated staged paths, cancellation, unavailable Git, process cleanup, keyboard, focus and screen readers. A JSON parse is syntax evidence only; it does not establish conformance or native behavior. Conflicts, unsafe renames and HEAD-dependent actions without HEAD refuse rather than act broadly. Native tests must prove stash-added files become untracked and that picking an older stash never removes the newer one; neither result follows merely from omitting `--index`.
